turns.response_html: Okay, here's the text from your screen: "Live with Gemini. In Linear B records, Eritha is associated with the syllabic transcription 'Ma-ki-ta,' of Sphagianes. Scholars categorised by modern scholars into the Eb, Ep, and Eo series, which record landholdings at the site, believed to have been a religious centre near Pylos, and may have shared a location with the large cemetery at Volimidia, around 4 kilometres northeast of the palace at Pylos. Most of the landholders at Sphagianes, including Eritha, are described with titles associated with religious cult, particularly forty-six people labelled as 'servants of the god.' The site was dedicated to a mother goddess and was possibly the chief goddess of the Pylian pantheon. Eritha has been named by Dimitris Nakassis as constituting around 2 percent of the estimated population of the polity. Dimitris Nakassis has argued that they represent 'a broad elite group' within it. Eritha is one of two women named as possible locations or some key sites within the Pylian state."

Okay, here's the rest of the text on your screen: "...religious organizations in the Pylian state were involved in holding office, along with another named Karpathia. Both were based at Sphagiana; Eritha appears to have been the more important of the two. Guy Middleton has argued that Eritha may have been a member of an aristocratic or royal family, but equally may have owed her authority to a religious system with little direct correspondence to the ruling palatial system."
